claims.text: Cache invalidation: removing a cached copy when its source data changes, so the next read is a miss and loads the new value.
claims.source_hint: content/glossary.yaml: cache-invalidation; Microsoft Azure Architecture Center: Cache-Aside pattern, 'Lifetime of cached data' / invalidating

claims.text: StackExchange.Redis IDatabase.KeyDeleteAsync asks Redis to delete the key and its value (against Redis 8 it sends UNLINK, which removes the key like DEL).
claims.source_hint: SE.Redis release notes 2.0.571 (KeyDeleteAsync uses UNLINK); Redis docs: commands/unlink, commands/del

claims.text: Redis does not read PostgreSQL or notice changes in the products table: in Đơn Hàng, product:{id} is replaced or removed only by ProductCache or when its TTL expires.
claims.source_hint: Redis docs: key expiration (EXPIRE/TTL); cache-aside lesson claim on Redis knowing nothing about PostgreSQL

claims.text: ProductsController.UpdatePrice is PATCH api/v1/products/{id:int} with [Authorize(Policy = "StaffOnly")]; it calls products.UpdatePriceAsync(id, request.PriceVnd), answers NotFound() for null, else Ok(ProductDto) with the new price.
ProductCache.UpdatePriceAsync first awaits inner.UpdatePriceAsync (the save), and only when it returns a product calls RemoveAsync("product:{id}"); for null (no such product) nothing is deleted.

EfProductRepository.UpdatePriceAsync finds the product with db.Products.FindAsync, sets PriceVnd and awaits SaveChangesAsync; if the save throws, the exception leaves ProductCache.UpdatePriceAsync before RemoveAsync runs.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Infrastructure/EfProductRepository.cs; C# await exception propagation

claims.text: If the key were deleted before the save, a read in between would miss, load the old price from PostgreSQL and SET it into Redis with a new 5-minute TTL.
claims.source_hint: ProductCache.cs @ stage-2: FindAsync (miss -> inner.FindAsync -> SetAsync with Ttl); comment at ProductCache.cs:52-53

claims.text: Saving first does not close every gap: if product:{id} is missing (e.g. TTL just ended), a read that loaded the old price before the save can write it after the delete, back until the TTL ends; UpdatePriceAsync takes no lock.
claims.source_hint: ProductCache.cs @ stage-2: FindAsync vs UpdatePriceAsync (no shared lock); Redis docs: SET creates the key if missing

claims.text: ProductCache.Ttl is TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5), with the comment that it is the longest a stale copy can live even if a delete is missed; SetAsync stores every copy with this TTL.

RemoveAsync calls KeyDeleteAsync inside try/catch for RedisException or RedisTimeoutException, logs 'Redis delete of {Key} failed; the old copy lives until its TTL ends', and does not rethrow, so the PATCH still answers 200.
Only changes through ProductCache.UpdatePriceAsync delete the key; a price changed directly in PostgreSQL with psql (PostgreSQL's command-line client) leaves product:{id} in Redis until its TTL ends.
claims.source_hint: ProductCache.cs @ stage-2 is the only RemoveAsync caller; PostgreSQL 17 docs: psql (interactive terminal)

claims.text: cache-invalidation.sh: staff token for lan.do@example.com via scripts/lib/keycloak.sh; redis() runs redis-cli (Redis's command-line client) in the redis container; base is the API's /api/v1 URL; curl -w prints the status code.
Script output at stage-2: first GET 890000 and 200 with product:3 filled; PATCH answers 200 with 950000; EXISTS product:3 prints 0; the next GET answers 950000 and product:3 holds 950000.
Redis EXISTS with one key returns 1 if the key exists and 0 if it does not.

After cache-invalidation.sh ends, `docker compose exec -T redis redis-cli EXISTS product:3` prints 0 unless product 3 was read in between, because the script's final PATCH to 890000 deleted the key again.

With a cache in front, keeping a TTL as an upper bound on staleness is worth it even when every update deletes the key, because deletes can be missed (Redis down, a late write, changes outside the API).
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Azure Architecture Center: Cache-Aside pattern, 'Lifetime of cached data' and 'Consistency'

claims.text: ProductsController.UpdatePrice does not reference Redis or ProductCache; it only sees IProductRepository, which the DI registration resolves to a ProductCache around EfProductRepository.
The StaffOnly policy (RequireRole("staff")) lets the PATCH through only for a token whose roles include staff.
Only GET /api/v1/products/{id} (ProductsController.Get) reads through ProductCache and asks Redis first; the list GET /api/v1/products reads DonHangDbContext directly.
